reasons.plausibility: The mechanism is physically inconsistent: Sn addition is proposed to induce an FCC-to-BCC transformation at high temperature, yet the hypothesis simultaneously claims an increase in the Curie temperature of the FCC phase, and the link between this transformation and coercivity increase is not justified.
reasons.testability: The test is vague: it does not specify the Sn amounts, the measurement temperature relative to the transformation, or how phase composition will be measured, and the falsification criterion ignores the possibility that a BCC phase forms but coercivity still does not increase.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is not useful because it proposes a mechanism (FCC-to-BCC transformation at high temperature) that contradicts the goal of overcoming coercivity limitations in single-phase FCC alloys and provides no credible pathway to a room-temperature coercivity increase.
